\[
X_4 = X_1 \cup \left( (X_2 \oplus H) \cap A \right)^{(n)}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(n\): The spur length
- \(H\): The 3 x 3 square

X_1 is A with its end points removed n times. This deletes every branch up to n pixels long and shortens the main lines by n. X_2 holds the end points of X_1. They grow back n times with the 3 x 3 square H, but only inside A, which restores the ends of the main lines. X_4 joins both. The four steps follow Gonzalez and Woods. The end point rule is this filter's own. A pixel is an end point when its neighbors are one corner pixel alone, or one side pixel with none, one or both of the corners next to it. All end points go at once in each removal step.
